First order intestate successors
First order intestate successors are the descendants of a bequeather.
If at the time of death of a bequeather a descendant of the bequeather is alive, the descendants of that relative who are related to the bequeather through him or her shall not succeed.

Spouse as intestate successor

If at the time of opening of a succession the father or mother of the bequeather is not alive, the descendants of the deceased parent replace him or her according to the provisions concerning first order successors.

ACT
105.
Size of compulsory portion
A compulsory portion is one-half of the value of the share of an estate which a successor would have received in the case of intestate succession if all intestate successors would have accepted the succession. The persons who renounce a succession by a contract shall not be taken into account upon determining the size of a compulsory portion.
If a person entitled to claim a compulsory portion has been bequeathed a share of an estate which is smaller than a compulsory portion, he or she may claim the deficient share as a compulsory portion from the co-successors.
If one from several successors has the right to receive a compulsory portion, he or she may refuse to satisfy the claim of some other person entitled to compulsory portion to such extent that he or she would receive his or her compulsory portion. Other successors shall be liable for the deficit.
If a legacy is given to a person entitled to a compulsory portion, he or she has a claim for the compulsory portion only in case he or she renounces the legacy. If the value of a legacy is lower than a compulsory portion, the person may claim a compulsory portion from the successors to the extent which he or she received less as legacy than he or she would have received as a compulsory portion.', 'Country: Estonia | Law: Inheritance | Civil code article 106
ACT
106.
Value of estate
Determination of the size of a compulsory portion shall be based on the property which forms part of the estate as at the date of opening of the succession.
In the specification of the compulsory portion, provisional successions, the spouse’s preferential share and gifts made by the bequeather to other persons within the last three years before the death of the bequeather for the purpose of reducing the compulsory portion shall also be considered part of the estate.
In the specification of the compulsory portion, the burial expenses of the bequeather, expenditure for preparation of an inventory of the estate and valuation of the estate, and one month’s maintenance expenditure for persons who were maintained by the bequeather shall not be considered part of the estate.
In the specification of the compulsory portion, the rights and obligations depending on a suspensive condition shall not be considered part of the estate. The rights and obligations depending on a resolutive condition shall be taken into account as nonconditional. Upon the fulfilment of the condition a set-off corresponding to the changed legal situation shall be made.', 'Country: Estonia | Law: Inheritance | Civil code article 173
ACT
173.
Certificate of recipient of compulsory portion
A notary shall authenticate a certificate concerning the claim arising from a compulsory portion (hereinafter certificate of recipient of compulsory portion) on the basis of a notarially authenticated application of the successor, the executor of the will or the person entitled to a compulsory portion.
The certificate of recipient of compulsory portion shall set out the recipient and the size of the compulsory portion as a legal share of the estate.']
response: In Estonia the compulsory portion equals **one‑half of the value of the share that a successor would have received under intestate succession (assuming all intestate heirs accepted the succession)**; persons who have renounced the succession are excluded from the calculation [S1].
reference: Under § 105 of the Estonian Law of Succession Act the compulsory portion is one half of the value of the share of the estate that the successor would have received in intestate succession if all intestate successors had accepted the succession. ['Country: Estonia | Law: Divorce | Civil code article 27
27.
Separate property
Joint property does not include the separate property of neither of the spouses.
The separate property of a spouse includes:
1) personal effects of the spouse;
2) objects which were in the ownership of the spouse before the marriage or objects acquired by the spouse during the marriage by disposal without charge, including as a gift or by succession;
3) objects which the spouse acquires on the basis of a right belonging to his or her separate property or as compensation for the destruction of, damage to or seizure of objects included in his or her separate property or on the basis of a transaction entered into with regard to his or her separate property;
4) units of a mandatory pension fund, money in the pension investment account and financial assets acquired for the money, including the proprietary rights arising from the contract entered into upon acquisition of such financial assets, and the proprietary rights arising from the insurance contract for a mandatory funded pension.
The expenses incurred by both spouses in the form of work and proprietary performance during jointness of property in order to receive benefit from the property (necessary and useful expenses) are not included in separate property. The value of such expenses shall be included in the joint property of the spouses.
Single objects or certain type of objects may be declared to be joint property or separate property by a marital property contract.', 'Country: Estonia | Law: Divorce | Civil code article 25
25
Joint property
In the case of jointness of property, the objects and other proprietary rights of the spouses acquired during the jointness of property shall transfer into the joint ownership of the spouses (hereinafter joint property).', 'Country: Estonia | Law: Divorce | Civil code article 28
28.
Principles of joint administration of joint property
(1) Unless otherwise agreed, spouses shall jointly exercise the rights and perform the obligations relating to joint property. Spouses have the right to possess jointly the objects forming part of their joint property.
(2) Spouses may transfer the right to administer joint property to one of the spouses by a marital property contract.
(3) Spouses shall administer joint property in the interests of matrimonial cohabitation and regular management of the property. They shall inform each other of the acts of administration of property and of the financial status.
(4) A spouse may require conclusion of transactions necessary for correction of an entry concerning an object included in the joint property to be entered in the register.']
reference: Under the Estonian Family Law Act, in the regime of jointness of property the objects and proprietary rights acquired by the spouses during the jointness become their joint property (§ 25). Separate property is excluded from it (§ 27): personal effects, objects owned before the marriage or acquired during the marriage without charge (gift or succession), objects acquired on the basis of or as compensation for separate property, and mandatory pension fund units.
